"""Pydantic models shared by the plan loader, runner and event log."""

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator

from harness.config import Tier

TaskStatus = Literal["pending", "running", "verifying", "done", "failed", "blocked"]


class _Strict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class ContextItem(_Strict):
    label: str
    content: str


class Budget(_Strict):
    max_turns: int = Field(ge=1)
    max_attempts: int = Field(ge=1)


class WorkOrder(_Strict):
    id: str
    title: str
    goal: str
    tier: Tier
    depends_on: list[str]
    files_owned: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    files_readonly: list[str]
    context: list[ContextItem]
    steps: list[str]
    constraints: list[str]
    acceptance: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    budget: Budget
    out_of_scope: list[str]

    @field_validator("id")
    @classmethod
    def _normalize_id(cls, value: str) -> str:
        ...


class Plan(_Strict):
    stage: str
    orders: list[WorkOrder]


class Usage(_Strict):
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    cache_read_tokens: int = 0
    cache_creation_tokens: int = 0
    cost_usd: float = 0.0


class TaskState(_Strict):
    task_id: str
    status: TaskStatus = "pending"
    attempts: int = 0
    tier_used: Tier | None = None
    usage: Usage = Field(default_factory=Usage)


class Event(_Strict):
    ts: datetime = Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))
    run_id: str
    task_id: str | None = None
    type: str
    payload: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

orders.title: Add the git worktree manager
orders.goal: src/harness/worktree.py gives each task its own branch and worktree, merges finished work back by rebase + fast-forward, reports conflicts without losing the worktree, and cleans up a run. Only subprocess git is used.

context.label: src/harness/worktree.py interface (implement every `...` and docstring)
context.content:
"""Git worktrees for parallel tasks: create, commit, merge back, clean up."""

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

MergeResult = Literal["merged", "conflict"]


class WorktreeError(RuntimeError):
    """A git command failed in a way the caller must handle."""


def _git(*args: str, cwd: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]: ...


class WorktreeManager:
    def __init__(self, repo: Path, run_id: str, integration_branch: str = "main") -> None: ...

    def branch(self, task_id: str) -> str:
        """harness/<run_id>/<task_id>"""

    def path(self, task_id: str) -> Path:
        """<repo>/.harness/worktrees/<task_id>"""

    def create(self, task_id: str, base: str | None = None) -> Path:
        """git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <base or integration_branch>. Raise WorktreeError
        (with git's stderr) if git fails, e.g. the branch or path already exists. Return the path."""

    def commit(self, task_id: str, message: str) -> bool:
        """git add -A, then commit in the worktree. Return False (and commit nothing) if there
        are no staged changes (`git diff --cached --quiet` exits 0), True after committing."""

    def merge(self, task_id: str) -> MergeResult:
        """In the worktree: git rebase <integration_branch>. On failure: git rebase --abort and
        return "conflict". Then in <repo>: git merge --ff-only <branch>; raise WorktreeError if
        that fails. Return "merged"."""

    def cleanup(self) -> None:
        """git worktree remove --force every worktree under <repo>/.harness/worktrees (from
        `git worktree list --porcelain`), delete every branch under refs/heads/harness/<run_id>/
        (git branch -D), then git worktree prune."""

context.label: decision
context.content:
- One WorktreeManager per run. Branch name: harness/<run_id>/<task_id>. Worktree path: <repo>/.harness/worktrees/<task_id>.
- The main checkout at <repo> must have the integration branch checked out; merge() fast-forwards it there.
- create() makes sure `.harness/` is listed in <git-common-dir>/info/exclude (append the line once if missing), so worktrees never show up as untracked files. Get the dir with `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (relative to repo if not absolute).
- merge() requires a clean worktree. If `git status --porcelain` in the worktree prints anything, raise WorktreeError("uncommitted changes in <task_id>").
- On rebase conflict: run `git rebase --abort` in the worktree, leave the worktree and branch in place, return "conflict".
- Paths from git may be resolved through symlinks (macOS /var -> /private/var); compare paths with Path.resolve() on both sides.
- Use subprocess.run([...], cwd=..., capture_output=True, text=True, check=False) through one helper; never shell=True; no GitPython or other library.

context.label: tests/test_worktree.py helper to use (copy exactly)
context.content:
def _repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()
    for args in (
        ["init", "-b", "main"],
        ["config", "user.email", "test@example.com"],
        ["config", "user.name", "Test"],
    ):
        subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True)
    (repo / "README.md").write_text("line one\n")
    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", "init"], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True)
    return repo

orders.title: Load and validate plan files and compute waves
orders.goal: load_plan(path) turns plan.json into a Plan or raises PlanError with a clear message for duplicate ids, unknown dependencies, cycles, blank acceptance commands and two orders in the same wave owning the same file. compute_waves gives the parallel waves the scheduler will run.

context.label: src/harness/plan.py interface (implement every `...`)
context.content:
"""Load a plan file and check it: ids, dependencies, cycles, ownership, acceptance."""

import json
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

from pydantic import ValidationError

from harness.models import Plan


class PlanError(ValueError):
    """The plan file is invalid. The message says why."""


def load_plan(path: Path) -> Plan: ...


def validate_plan(plan: Plan) -> list[list[str]]: ...


def compute_waves(plan: Plan) -> list[list[str]]: ...

context.label: decision: exact behaviour and error messages
context.content:
load_plan(path): read the file as UTF-8 JSON. json.JSONDecodeError -> PlanError("invalid JSON: <msg>"). Plan.model_validate(data); ValidationError -> PlanError(f"invalid plan: {err}"). Then call validate_plan(plan) and return the plan. Re-raise with `from err`.

validate_plan(plan) runs these checks in this order and raises PlanError at the first failure; on success it returns compute_waves(plan):
1. duplicate ids      -> "duplicate id: <id>"
2. unknown deps       -> "unknown dependency: <order id> depends on <dep>"
3. blank acceptance   -> "empty acceptance: <order id>"   (any command that is empty after .strip())
4. cycles             -> raised by compute_waves
5. overlapping files_owned within one wave -> "overlapping files_owned in wave <n>: <path> (<id a>, <id b>)"; compare paths as str(PurePosixPath(p)) so "./a.py" == "a.py"; waves are numbered from 1.

compute_waves(plan): level-by-level topological sort. Wave 1 = orders with no depends_on; each next wave = orders whose deps are all in earlier waves. Ids sorted alphabetically within a wave. If orders remain but none can be placed -> PlanError("cycle: <remaining ids sorted, joined by ', '>"). Assumes deps are known (validate_plan checks that first).

orders.title: Add the JSONL event log and `harness events`
orders.goal: Every state change can be recorded with EventLog.emit() as one JSON line in <run_dir>/events.jsonl, safely from many concurrent async tasks, and `harness events RUN_DIR [--follow]` prints the log. This is what the future UI reads.

context.content:
"""Append-only JSONL event log for a run: <run_dir>/events.jsonl."""

import asyncio
import time
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from harness.models import Event

EVENTS_FILE = "events.jsonl"


class EventLog:
    def __init__(self, run_dir: Path, run_id: str) -> None:
        """Create run_dir (parents too) if missing. self.path = run_dir / EVENTS_FILE.
        self.run_id = run_id. One asyncio.Lock per instance."""

    async def emit(
        self, type: str, task_id: str | None = None, payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> Event:
        """Build Event(run_id, task_id, type, payload or {}). Under the lock, open self.path in
        append mode (UTF-8), write event.model_dump_json() + "\n" in one write() call, flush.
        Return the event."""


def read_events(path: Path) -> list[Event]:
    """Parse every non-blank line with Event.model_validate_json, in file order."""


def follow(path: Path, poll_interval: float = 0.5) -> Iterator[str]:
    """Wait until path exists, yield every existing line (without the newline), then keep
    yielding new complete lines as they are appended, sleeping poll_interval between polls.
    Never returns. Skip blank lines."""

from typer.testing import CliRunner

from harness.cli import app
from harness.config import MODEL_IDS, TIER_LADDER

runner = CliRunner()


def test_help_lists_commands():
    result = runner.invoke(app, ["--help"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0
    for name in ("run", "status", "report", "validate"):
        assert name in result.output


def test_every_tier_has_a_model():
    assert TIER_LADDER == ("haiku", "sonnet", "opus")
    assert set(MODEL_IDS) == set(TIER_LADDER)
